title: kernel-cascade-chronicle-2026-12
body:
Summary:

This is a working note for a focused exploration into kernel-cascade relationships observed in long-running inference traces. Different from our usual occupancy snapshots, this probe attempts to quantify "Cascade Depth" and "Sync Stall Fraction" across mixed microbatch traffic and CUDA graph replay paths.

Motivation:
- We see recurring tail-latency events where a short host-side stall (copy/pin/descriptor update) precedes an extended tail in multiple small kernels.
- Hypothesis: those tails are not single-kernel inefficiencies but emergent artifacts of tightly-coupled kernel cascades where later kernels wait on partial warps or fragmented sharedmem states.

Experiment setup:
- Model: opt-6.7b-like decoder run, seq-length 512, microbatch sizes {1,2,4}, mixed prompts (50/50 short/long).
- HW: g5.12xlarge equivalent (A100-sim), PCIe gen4 host path for controlled hostcopy jitter.
- Schedulers: current async-copy + cuda-graph replay enabled (persistent-graph path).
- Tooling: Nsight Systems (2026.4), Nsight Compute (2026.3) for spot checks, nvprof-style sampling via custom tracer for kernel start/stop and stream events.

Capture recipe (quick commands):
- record nsight sys: nsys profile --capture-range=manual --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt --output kernel_cascade_2026_12.qdrep --force-overwrite 
- start at host trace boundary, run steady state for 3000 requests, then stop capture.
- extract timeline: nsys export --report=timeline --input kernel_cascade_2026_12.qdrep --output timeline.csv

Custom tracer notes:
- We added a micro-bucketed timestamp for every kernel push (host enqueue time, driver launch latency, kernel start, kernel end, stream sync).
- Label kernels by spot: prefetch/kv-decode/attn-matmul/ffn/finalize.

New metrics defined for this probe:
- Cascade Depth: integer count of how many discrete kernels launch on the critical path before the final blocking sync for a token increment. Measured per-request and aggregated as p50/p95/p99.
- Sync Stall Fraction: total time spent in explicit stream/synchronization APIs (cudaStreamSynchronize, cudaMemcpy blocking) divided by end-to-end request time.
- Warp Lifetime Census: distribution of warp-active durations inside a kernel (bucketed ms) to detect large tail of warps that run much longer than median.

Key observations (first pass):
- Median Cascade Depth for mixed-microbatch workload = 6; p99 = 12. Many high-depth traces coincide with short hostcopy bursts (0.5-2ms).
- Sync Stall Fraction correlates with p99 latency (Spearman 0.72). Most sync time occurs in small cudaMemcpyAsync -> implicit synchronize patterns when graph replay merges non-contiguous memory writes.
- Warp Lifetime Census shows bimodal distribution in attn kernels: majority finish ~0.12ms but a long tail at 1.1ms and 3.3ms, indicating straggler warps likely due to bank conflicts / divergent control flow on long sequences.

Interesting timeline patterns:
- Cascade cascade: sequence where prefetch kernel (K1) launches, followed by small descriptor update kernel (K2), then fused-attn (K3) which depends on K1 KV buffer ready; if K2 stalls on hostcopy, K3 starts but runs fragmented warps leading to extended runtime, preventing downstream ffn kernels from overlapping. Visual pattern: many narrow spikes (K1,K2) then a fat plateau (K3).
- Graph replay edge case: when the graph includes multiple conditional nodes, replay path can schedule a no-op kernel with zero active threads but still serialize stream events, increasing apparent Cascade Depth without useful work.

Spot-check Nsight Compute anchors:
- For an attn-kernel tail sample (trace id T-204): sm_efficiency drops from 92% (median window) to 14% in tail window; L1 bank conflict counters (shared_load_conflicts) jump 8x.
- Registers per-thread stable; not a register spill. Warp divergence flags show increased divergent-branch percentage in tail.

Hypotheses and interpretations:
1) Hostcopy jitter causes short gaps that fragment kernel scheduling; fragmented kernels have smaller active warp sets and suffer from worse memory bank contention and lower tensor core utilization.
2) Implicit synchronizations in our graph materialization (due to host-managed conditionals) add artificial Cascade Depth, amplifying tail events even when individual kernels are efficient.

Actionable follow-ups (prioritized):
- Low effort (days): add micro-batching alignment to coalesce small hostcopy operations; change copy batching window from 2ms -> 6ms to reduce fragmentation.
- Medium effort (1-2 weeks): modify graph materializer to inline conditional no-op nodes into branchable kernels to avoid stream-level implicit synchronizations. See linear ticket INF-4821.
- Research spike (2 weeks): implement warp-coalescing shim in serving runtime which tries to schedule contiguous token work to same CTA/SM affinity to reduce warp tail fragmentation.

Quick TODOs / notes-to-self:
- Re-run capture with KV-prefetch disabled to isolate prefetch contribution to Cascade Depth.
- Add synthetic noise on hostcopy path (0.2ms jitter) and measure Cascade Depth sensitivity curve.
- Bring SRE + infra: verify PCIe topology differs across instances used for prod vs. lab; ensure we replicate NVLink vs. PCIe differences.

Rough metrics snapshot (CSV-ish, for quick paste into sheet):
request_type, microbatch, p50_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, median_cascade_depth, p99_cascade_depth, sync_stall_frac
short,1,22.4,98.1,4,9,0.07
long,1,44.7,215.3,7,14,0.19
mixed,2,28.1,150.2,6,12,0.14

Open questions:
- Are we seeing hardware-level preemption/interference from concurrent tenants (SM clock scaling) or is everything host-side? Need PMU traces across devices.
- Can we attribute long warp tails to specific input-length-dependent control flow (e.g., different attention mask shapes)?

Related artifacts and threads:
- INF-4821 (linear): kernel cascade analysis and graph materializer changes.
- PR #789: small graph-inlining prototype (tests under /bench/graph-inline/).
- Slack channel: #serving-runtime-profiling, thread: "cascade-census" (Oct-Nov 2026).

Appendix: quick capture pointers and caveats:
- Avoid sampling-only captures for this probe; we need accurate host enqueue timestamps (use nsys manual range).
- Watch out for driver-level stream priority behavior—if a helper maintenance stream has high priority it can preempt our graph and create false-positive cascade events.
- When exporting timeline to CSV, filter on correlation-id tag we add per-request to avoid noisy background kernels.

If helpful I can synthesize a small script to convert our timeline.csv into per-request Cascade Depth + Sync Stall time with CCS (custom trace parser). Will do next if team agrees.

End of notes.
